comments: Cross-review confirms that Client is applied consistently to the filename, declaration, constructor, and textual representation.
The oracle keeps the phone API and incorporates the right-side default value without mixing in the competing number rename.
getNumber and setNumber consistently implement the selected accessor-name resolution over the existing phone field.
Keeping the ancestral String representation is the stated coherent resolution of the incompatible Float and int changes.
The complete Person artifact is retained according to the stated resolution when the left branch removes its contents.
Both branches add the same Person implementation and the oracle reproduces the complete addition.
Email removal is propagated through the field, constructor, and accessors while the selected name state remains intact.
The compatible email and phone additions are represented in fields, constructor arguments, assignments, and accessors.
The oracle removes only the selected textual representation and retains the Person data API.
The four-argument constructor in the oracle has no source in base, left, or right; revise the oracle or add non-circular evidence that authorizes this invented API.
The oracle combines Builder-based creation and status persistence with Validator-based create and update checks.
OrderService depends on AuditLogger and four validator classes supplied by the branches, but all five helper artifacts are absent; include them and correct the source filename/type inconsistencies.
The selected decomposition into Individual and ContactInfo is complete and internally consistent; the competing whole-class rename cannot coexist without replacing the chosen identity type.
Contrary to the first review, the left-side name-to-fullName change can be propagated directly to PersonalInfo, but the oracle copies the right decomposition with name/getName/setName unchanged.
The left-side getPhoneNumber/setPhoneNumber rename is compatible with the decomposition but is not propagated to ContactInfo; the oracle is identical to the right branch.
ContactData receives the selected PhoneNumber representation while Person retains identity state, avoiding the left branch's apparent syntax defect.
Person.java declares and constructs public type PersonIdentity, violating the Java filename/type contract and failing the stated decision to retain Person consistently.
The empty base is resolved into the complete PersonBasicInfo and PersonContactInfo decomposition selected from the right branch.
Address removal is preserved while name is restored in CoreInfo and the contact fields remain in ExtendedInfo.
The email, phone, and social-media additions are preserved across the PersonId and PersonContact decomposition.
The left branch removes birthDate, but the oracle retains birthDate in Identity; propagate the removal through the selected decomposition.
The right-side BasicPerson/ExtendedPerson split is retained and the compatible left-side nationality addition is propagated to ExtendedPerson.
The complete strategy artifact set is present and dispatch is coherently combined with logging, unsupported-type handling, and exception logging.
The oracle combines Client and Location but drops city, although city exists in base and left Address and is moved to right Individual; preserve it in the resolved model.
The Person-to-User reorganization is selected while the complete ancestral Contact representation replaces the narrower PhoneContact artifact.
The selected Customer and Order field changes are present, but Custumer.java declares public class Customer; make the filename, public type, manifest, and oracle tree consistent.
Division and Worker consistently implement the selected coupled reorganization and remove the inherited Departament.java filename/type mismatch.
The oracle consistently applies the selected Person removal and retains Address rather than mixing in the competing DetailedAddress/Profile tree.
Employee is retained while Organization and Position incorporate the selected right-side decomposition responsibilities.
The selected Contact/Person model consistently propagates email removal instead of mixing it with the competing User/UserContact reorganization.
The oracle copies the right tree without mapping the compatible left additions Customer.email and Order.orderDate into Client and Purchase.
Course plus StudentDetails loses the student's identity fields even though id and name/fullName survive in both branches; add a resolved identity artifact and update the declared tree.
The oracle consistently selects Profile/User and preserves the left-side email and joinDate additions over the competing Account/UserProfile model.
The oracle is identical to the right branch and discards the left premium price tiers; combine tiered discounts with the MAX_DISCOUNT cap.
The 18-to-150 constraint subsumes the compatible left non-negative constraint and coherently resolves both validations.
Singleton access and reset coexist coherently with the public driver-aware constructor and complete factory API.
LinkedHashSet preserves uniqueness and deterministic order while defensive list and set views reconcile the incompatible getMembers return types.
Configurable exception/boolean handling integrates username, email, password, business, logging, and range validations from both branches.

Recurring configuration occurs after total calculation, so changed cycles and payment methods do not affect the current total; the oracle also invents unsupported compromise tax, hybrid bonuses, credit limits, and upgrade rules.
